questions.prompt: You are on the button, heads-up against the big blind, with top pair on a dry board. You bet small and get raised. A set or two pair is now more likely. You should…

choices.text: Continue only with the top of that hand, and fold the weaker top pairs to a large raise.
Always fold top pair, top kicker
Call any raise because you have top pair

questions.explanation: A raise on a dry board is stronger than a call. Kicker and price still matter. Top pair is not one action.

questions.prompt: Three players see a flop of 8h 7h 6c. You are under the gun with ace-high and no draw. Best default?

choices.text: Check and give up to a bet. Multiway and wet, ace-high is air.
Call a pot bet because an ace is coming

questions.explanation: You do not have a hand or a draw, and two players remain. This is a fold.

questions.prompt: Heads-up, in position, you have the nut flush draw and two overcards on a wet flop. Facing a small bet…

choices.text: Continue. You have a strong draw, not air.
Only continue if you are already ahead

questions.explanation: This is a high-equity draw. Calling or raising are both real. Folding is not.

questions.prompt: Out of position, multiway, you flop bottom pair. Someone bets and a player calls. You should…

choices.text: Fold. You are behind a bet and a call with a weak pair.
Call because the pot is big
Donk the turn no matter the card

questions.explanation: Bottom pair does not beat a bet-and-call on a multiway flop.
